title: Microsoft 365 admin center: high-usage Copilot users list in Billing & usage
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, existing licence-assignment routes and report privacy controls are supported. It distinguishes the planned high-usage page from the documented Credits report and keeps the new page's navigation, default, entitlement and purchase-action effects explicitly unresolved.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; front matter: changes
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this particular High-usage users page.
claims.quote: Searched: "557176" "High-usage users" Microsoft Learn Copilot; "Copilot" "High-usage users" "Billing" navigation default enable disable Microsoft 365 admin center. Opened Credits report, pay-as-you-go overview/setup and configure-copilot-admin-center; results describe other reports and controls.

claims.claim: The navigation path to the new High-usage users page is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "High-usage users" "Billing" navigation default enable disable Microsoft 365 admin center. Opened pay-as-you-go-setup-copilot and configure-copilot-admin-center; their routes concern billing policies, services and settings, not the High-usage users page.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The new page's default state is unknown; Microsoft has not stated automatic appearance or required administrator activation.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "High-usage users" "Billing" navigation default enable disable Microsoft 365 admin center. Read roadmap, pay-as-you-go overview/setup and Copilot settings. None states the page's arrival default; the documented pay-as-you-go billing default is a different fact.

claims.claim: Entitlement to this specific administrator page is not published, so its licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "High-usage users" Copilot licensing prerequisites price roles purchase assign licenses admin center; "High-usage users" "Copilot" license page entitlement charge price. Read billing setup, overview and licensing; general Copilot user licences do not state entitlement to this admin page.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licence or separate price specifically for this page is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: "High-usage users" "Copilot" license page entitlement charge price. Read pay-as-you-go overview/setup and billing-licensing; searched licence-options excerpts. These cover service and user licensing, not a separate licence or price for the High-usage users page.

claims.claim: The existing Credits report is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Reports > Microsoft Copilot > Credits.
claims.quote: In the navigation menu, select Reports. ... Select Usage. ... On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Credits.

claims.claim: The Credits report documentation includes preview qualifications.
claims.quote: During preview, the report displays a maximum of 30 days of Copilot Credits history.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The Credits report Alerts card appears when one or more users consume more than 3,000 credits in the past 30 days.
claims.quote: The Alerts card is visible in the report when one or more users consume more than 3,000 credits in the past 30 days.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: A similar Credits report alert appears for users consuming 2,000 to 3,000 credits.
claims.quote: If users consume 2,000 to 3,000 credits, a similar alert appears.

claims.claim: View Copilot credits details opens a user list that can be exported to CSV.
claims.quote: Select View Copilot credits details to see the user list and export it to CSV.

claims.claim: The Credits report covers users without a Microsoft Copilot licence interacting with metered agents in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: If you configure pay-as-you-go, and users without a Microsoft Copilot license use metered agents in Copilot Chat, the data appears in the report.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether the new page uses the Credits report's data or thresholds.
claims.quote: Searched: "High-usage users" "Copilot" conceal names thresholds data rollout; "557176" "High-usage users" Microsoft Learn Copilot. Read Credits report and billing setup; neither ties its data or alert windows to the new page. The roadmap gives only the new page's greater-than-2000 threshold.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Copilot pay-as-you-go service consumption is billed through the Azure subscription specified during billing setup.
claims.quote: When you use a Microsoft pay-as-you-go service linked to an Azure subscription, the service gets billed through the Azure subscription that you specified when you set up pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: The Azure subscription uses the Azure meter set up for the service.
claims.quote: The Azure subscription uses the Azure meter set up for the service.

claims.claim: The pay-as-you-go overview says billing is disabled by default for new pay-as-you-go features.
claims.quote: When Microsoft adds new features that use pay-as-you-go billing, it announces them in a message center post. ... By default, pay-as-you-go billing is disabled.

claims.claim: Classic answers by agents in Copilot Chat, Teams or SharePoint are not charged for Microsoft 365 Copilot licence holders when the agent runs with their authenticated identity.
claims.quote: If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged when the agent runs with your authenticated identity.

claims.claim: Generative answers by agents in Copilot Chat, Teams or SharePoint are not charged for Microsoft 365 Copilot licence holders when the agent runs with their authenticated identity.
claims.quote: If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged when the agent runs with your authenticated identity.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph tenant grounding by agents in Copilot Chat, Teams or SharePoint is not charged for Microsoft 365 Copilot licence holders when the agent runs with their authenticated identity.
claims.quote: If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged when the agent runs with your authenticated identity.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published whether this page's purchase action eliminates all of a listed user's charges.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot high usage users purchase license eliminates charges Microsoft 365 Copilot billing licensing. Read billing-licensing and pay-as-you-go overview/setup. They describe qualified licence-holder exemptions, not the effect of this particular page's purchase action on every listed charge.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Usage reports hide usernames, display names, groups and sites by default.
claims.quote: By default, all reports hide user information such as usernames, display names, groups, and sites to help companies support local privacy laws.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether the new High-usage users page follows the usage-report concealment setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "High-usage users" "Copilot" conceal names thresholds data rollout. Read usage reports overview and Credits report: both state concealment for usage reports, but neither identifies the planned Billing & usage page as one of those reports.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Showing identifiable user information in usage reports is logged in the Microsoft Purview portal audit log.
claims.quote: Showing identifiable user information is a logged event in the Microsoft Purview portal audit log.

claims.claim: The existing licence-assignment route is Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. ... Select a product. ... On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns an existing licence through Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Assigning licences in the existing Microsoft 365 admin center route requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The report privacy control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: Select Settings. ... Select Org Settings. ... On the Services tab, select Reports. ... In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/admin/reportSettings changes tenant report concealment through the displayConcealedNames request-body property.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/reportSettings ... displayConcealedNames ... If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Global administrators can change the usage-report concealment setting, including for the Credits report.
claims.quote: Global administrators can change the settings to show or hide the Billing Policy ID. ... Changes to this hidden data setting affect the username, display name, and Billing Policy ID.
